//: FOR `pnpm lint:boundaries` ONLY. Never used to compile anything.
It exists to make the boundary rules operate on a graph of SOURCE files. Without it,
dependency-cruiser resolves `@rc/core` the way Node does: through the pnpm symlink at
packages/<pkg>/node_modules/@rc/core, followed to its real target, landing on
packages/core/dist/index.js. That has two consequences and both are fatal to the rules:
1. Excluding build output — which any sane config does — then excludes every workspace
edge in the graph, because every one of them terminates in a `dist` path. The wall
rules had nothing to forbid. Verified: with an `@rc/simulator` import sitting in
packages/policy/src/ev.ts, dependency-cruiser reported that file as having ZERO
dependencies and the run passed clean.
2. NOT excluding build output puts compiled JS in the graph, where the parser fails
outright ('Unexpected template string') and no rule runs at all.
Mapping `@rc/*` to `packages/*/src` avoids both. The graph is source-to-source, `dist`
stays excluded, and `reachable: true` is evaluated over edges that exist.
Kept separate from tsconfig.base.json deliberately. Adding `paths` there would let a
developer import across packages without declaring the dependency, and the build would
accept it — trading one silently-disabled guarantee for another.
